gap: No result ChatGPT got states what named reviewers measured on these units: the EcoFlow DELTA 3 Max Plus delivered 1.64 kWh of its 2,048 Wh in StorageReview's discharge test (about 33 minutes at 3,000 W), and The Solar Lab's inverter-on idle draw runs from 8 W (Jackery HomePower 3000) through 12.8 W (BLUETTI Apex 200) and 20.5 W (Anker SOLIX F3000) to 37 W (Pecron F3000LFP).
standout_why: I opened rvgearlab.com (cited), powerstationsrated.com (cited), wattsift.com (cited), truewattlab.com (cited), powerstations.reviews/jackery-3000 (cited) and outagehouse.com. RV Gear Lab says 'Spec-sheet researched', Power Stations Rated says 'We don't run hands-on tests', and WattSift and powerstations.reviews carry no measured figure; powerstations.reviews computes runtime as rated Wh x 0.85. TrueWattLab has an 'Idle / Lab Eff.' column, but it names no measurer per figure and shows N/D (85% default) for the DELTA 3 Max Plus and Jackery Explorer 3000 v2; its filled rows are other models (Apex 300, DELTA Pro 3, F3800 Plus). Outagehouse's only measurement is OutdoorGearLab's 910 Wh for the Explorer 1000 v2, and it assumes 20 W standby for the rest. None gives a measured delivered-Wh or idle draw for the units ChatGPT recommended. It is not a 3 because the measurements mostly confirm ChatGPT's 85% arithmetic and do not overturn its pick.
decides: Confirms the pick with a caveat, and separates the 3,072 Wh backup options. The DELTA 3 Max Plus held 3,000 W and tripped only above about 3,800 W (AndroidGuys), but StorageReview got 1.64 kWh out of it (80%), so full-load runtime is nearer 33 minutes than ChatGPT's 35. For outage use with the inverter left on, 24 hours of idle costs 192 Wh on the Jackery HomePower 3000, 492 Wh on the Anker F3000 and 888 Wh (29% of the battery) on the Pecron F3000LFP, which favours the Jackery over the Anker ChatGPT named for backup and counts against the Pecron despite its price. Of ours, the BLUETTI Apex 200 has the best measured efficiency in the set (90%, The Solar Lab) and 12.8 W idle; 2,560 Wh x 0.90 is about 2,304 Wh, roughly 40% more than the Max Plus's measured 1.64 kWh. That supports it as an efficiency/low-idle segment pick, subject to the brief's mid-Feb 2027 ship date, which I did not reread. I found no named measurement for the ALLPOWERS R3500 or Growatt HELIOS 3600, so this angle cannot rank them.

findings.source_title: EcoFlow DELTA 3 Max Plus & Ultra Plus Review (StorageReview)

findings.source_title: EcoFlow DELTA 3 Max Plus & Ultra Plus Review (StorageReview)
findings.note: Quarch Mains Power Analysis Module; fully charged unit with a workstation connected, incoming power removed. Published 2025-09-30. EcoFlow's claim is under 10 ms.

findings.label: Measured AC and DC energy delivered (AndroidGuys)
findings.value: AC about 1,740 Wh (roughly 85%); DC about 1,830 Wh (just over 89%)
findings.note: Scott Webster, published 2026-02-09. Test setup not described; he calls the result unofficial. 1,740 / 3,000 W = 34.8 min. The two reviewers differ: 80% (StorageReview) against 85% (AndroidGuys).

findings.label: Output held and trip point (AndroidGuys)
findings.value: Held a 3,000 W load for an extended period; did not trip until the load exceeded roughly 3,800 W
findings.note: Scott Webster, 2026-02-09. Duration of the 3,000 W run not given. Fan noise is described only as 'mid twenties' dB at light load and 'low forties' near 3,000 W, with no method or distance.

findings.product: EcoFlow DELTA 3 Ultra Plus (same 3,072 Wh / 3,600 W class as the DELTA 3 Ultra ChatGPT showed)
findings.label: Measured energy delivered on full discharge (StorageReview)
findings.value: 2.61 kWh of 3,072 Wh rated, about 85%; 3.54 kWh to recharge (about 87%); UPS transfer 8.25 ms
findings.source_title: EcoFlow DELTA 3 Max Plus & Ultra Plus Review (StorageReview)
findings.note: Dylan Dougherty, 2025-09-30. The unit tested is the Ultra Plus, not the plain Ultra; treat it as a proxy only. 2,610 Wh / 3,000 W = 52 min, matching ChatGPT's estimate.

findings.label: Measured usable AC energy at two loads (Notebookcheck)
findings.value: About 2,500 Wh at a 200 W load (81%); almost 2,800 Wh at a continuous 1,800 W load (91%)
findings.source_title: Powerhouse with 3.6 kW and 3 kWh: Anker Solix F3000 review (Notebookcheck)
findings.note: Marcus Schwarten, published 2026-02-20, updated 2026-10-05. European 230 V unit, not the US 120 V model. Efficiency rises with load, so a flat 85% overstates light-load runtime: 2,500 Wh / 200 W = 12.5 h against ChatGPT's 13 h.

findings.label: Measured AC charge time, energy and noise (Notebookcheck)
findings.value: Full charge in 1:20 h using 3,480 Wh from the wall (88% reached the battery); about 35 dB at 1 m at a good 3,000 W AC output
findings.source_title: Powerhouse with 3.6 kW and 3 kWh: Anker Solix F3000 review (Notebookcheck)
findings.note: European 230 V unit; a US 120 V outlet limits charge power, so the 1:20 h figure may not carry over to the US model.

findings.label: Measured inverter efficiency and idle draw (The Solar Lab)
findings.value: Around 84% inverter efficiency; 20.5 W idle draw
findings.source_title: Anker SOLIX F3000 review (The Solar Lab)
findings.note: Idle: fully charged, AC inverter on, nothing connected, calculated over three tests; 4.5 W under Anker's 25 W claim. 20.5 W x 24 h = 492 Wh, 16% of 3,072 Wh. The page shows no author or date, only 'Copyright 2026'.

findings.label: Output held per outlet (The Solar Lab)
findings.value: Full 3,600 W from the 30 A RV (TT-30) plug; 2,400 W continuous from the main AC outlets
findings.source_title: Anker SOLIX F3000 review (The Solar Lab)
findings.note: Backs ChatGPT's per-outlet caveat with a test: the full 3,600 W came only from the RV outlet. Page undated.

findings.label: Measured idle draw (The Solar Lab)
findings.source_title: Jackery HomePower 3000 Review: Is Jackery's First "HomePower" Unit a Good Purchase? (The Solar Lab)
findings.note: The Solar Lab calls it the best it has seen from a large power station. Load and method are not stated on the page. 8 W x 24 h = 192 Wh, 6% of 3,072 Wh. The page gives no measured efficiency or usable Wh, and no author or date beyond 'Copyright 2026'.

findings.label: Measured efficiency and idle draw (The Solar Lab)
findings.source_title: BLUETTI Apex 200 Review: A Powerful and Smart Expandable Power Station (The Solar Lab)
findings.note: Idle with the inverter on and nothing drawing from the AC outlets; the efficiency test load is not stated. 2,560 Wh x 0.90 = about 2,304 Wh (my arithmetic, not a measured Wh). 12.8 W x 24 h = 307 Wh. Page undated.

findings.label: Measured AC charge time and input (The Solar Lab)
findings.value: Full charge in about 2 h 21 min from a standard wall outlet at 1,800 W; reached the full 3,000 W solar input using both solar ports
findings.source_title: BLUETTI Apex 200 Review: A Powerful and Smart Expandable Power Station (The Solar Lab)
findings.note: The review also says the inverter 'easily exceeded' its advertised 3,600 W surge, with no figure. Page undated.

findings.label: Measured efficiency, idle draw and output (The Solar Lab)
findings.value: 83% average efficiency at a sustained 3,600 W; 37 W idle draw; 4,500 W held about 10 s before tripping
findings.source_title: Pecron F3000LFP portable power station review (The Solar Lab)
findings.note: Efficiency: full to empty at 3,600 W. Idle: charged to 100%, drained with only the inverter on, then calculated. 37 W x 24 h = 888 Wh, 29% of 3,072 Wh. AC charge 'just over two hours' at 1,800 W. Page undated.

findings.label: Reviewer's discharge estimate (DroneXL)
findings.value: About 1,720 Wh, 84%; two space heaters at 2,100 W for 50 min 25 s; a 3,300 W load tripped the AC breaker
findings.note: Russ (51 Drones), published 2025-07-02. He calls it an estimate; 2,100 W x 0.840 h is 1,765 Wh, so his 1,720 Wh does not quite reconcile. Weak measurement: use only with that caveat. The 29 dB noise figure in the article is not presented as his own reading.

findings.label: What the pages ChatGPT got say about testing
findings.value: None of the six rival pages I opened ran its own tests; three say so outright
findings.source_title: Best 3000W Portable Power Station of 2026 (Power Stations Rated)
findings.note: Power Stations Rated: 'We don't run hands-on tests'. RV Gear Lab (https://www.rvgearlab.com/power-electrical/best-3000-watt-portable-power-station, updated 2026-10-02): 'Spec-sheet researched'. Outagehouse (https://outagehouse.com/compare/best-3000w-power-station/): 'we have not tested them'. powerstations.reviews/jackery-3000: 'Runtime is rated capacity x 0.85 / watts'.

unsourced: ALLPOWERS R3500: a named reviewer's measured usable Wh, efficiency or idle draw. Search turned up only exspenditure.com (a claimed ~3,200 Wh usable, above the 3,168 Wh rating) and batteryskills.com; I opened neither and would not rely on them. The 65.7 lb / 93 lb weight conflict is also unresolved.
Growatt HELIOS 3600: any named measurement of usable capacity, efficiency or idle draw. Search returned only spec sheets and batteryskills.com.
Jackery HomePower 3000: measured usable Wh or efficiency. The Solar Lab gives only the 8 W idle; the TechRadar Explorer 3000 v2 review appeared in search but I did not open it.
EcoFlow DELTA 3 Max Plus and DELTA 3 Ultra: measured idle draw. Neither StorageReview nor AndroidGuys reports one, and I found no Solar Lab review of either.
EcoFlow DELTA 3 Ultra (non-Plus): its own measured discharge. Only the Ultra Plus was tested by StorageReview.
DJI Power 2000: a metered full-discharge figure and idle draw from a lab-style reviewer. Only DroneXL's estimate was found.
Anker SOLIX F3000 US 120 V model: measured usable Wh. Notebookcheck tested the EU 230 V unit; The Solar Lab gives a percentage only.

BLUETTI Apex 200: Electrek's 10.5 W idle with the display off, and a 34 W idle for the Pecron F3000LFP on a Solar Lab quiz page, appeared only in search summaries. I did not open those pages, so they are not in findings.

Publication dates for The Solar Lab reviews: the pages show no author or date, only 'Copyright 2026 The Solar Lab'. Its how-to pages do not document the test method either; the method notes above come from the individual reviews.
Dabbsson 3000L and Mango Power E: named measurements were not searched; the call budget ran out.
Prices: none were read in this run. The tool calls went to measurements, so every price for these candidates needs a fresh read by another angle.
